#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI tool that prints sanitized versions of filenames.

Usage:
    python sanitize.py [--check] FILE [FILE ...]

Sanitization rules:
  - Unicode is normalized with NFKD and non-ascii characters dropped.
  - The name is lowercased.
  - Runs of spaces/punctuation are collapsed to a single hyphen
    (leading/trailing hyphens on the stem are stripped).
  - The file extension is preserved.
  - Dotfiles without an extension (e.g. .bashrc) pass through unchanged.

With --check, nothing is printed; the exit code is 1 if any input would
change, 0 otherwise.
"""

import argparse
import re
import sys
import unicodedata


def _clean_stem(stem: str) -> str:
    # Normalize unicode, dropping characters that have no ascii form.
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", stem)
    text = text.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    # Lowercase.
    text = text.lower()
    # Collapse runs of spaces/punctuation to a single hyphen.
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9-]+", "-", text)
    # Tidy up hyphens at the edges of the stem.
    text = text.strip("-")
    return text


def sanitize(name: str) -> str:
    """Return the sanitized version of *name*."""
    stem, ext = name.rsplit(".", 1) if "." in name else (name, "")
    if ext:
        ext = "." + _clean_stem(ext)
        return _clean_stem(stem) + ext
    # No extension: dotfiles like .bashrc pass through untouched.
    if name.startswith("."):
        return name
    return _clean_stem(name)


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Sanitize filenames.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check",
        action="store_true",
        help="exit 1 if any input would change, 0 otherwise; print nothing",
    )
    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="+", help="filenames to sanitize")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    changed = False
    for name in args.files:
        safe = sanitize(name)
        if safe != name:
            changed = True
        if not args.check:
            print(safe)
    return 1 if (args.check and changed) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from sanitize import sanitize


def run_cli(*args):
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "sanitize.py", *args],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("raw", "expected"),
    [
        # Already clean names pass through unchanged.
        ("report.pdf", "report.pdf"),
        ("my-file_v2.txt", "my-file_v2.txt"),
        # Lowercasing.
        ("Report Final.PDF", "report-final.pdf"),
        ("CAMELCase.TXT", "camelcase.txt"),
        # Spaces collapse to a single hyphen.
        ("my file.txt", "my-file.txt"),
        ("my    file.txt", "my-file.txt"),
        # Runs of punctuation collapse to a single hyphen.
        ("weird!!name??here.txt", "weird-name-here.txt"),
        ("a & b (final).docx", "a-b-final.docx"),
        # Spaces and punctuation mixed together collapse to one hyphen.
        ("hello ,; world.md", "hello-world.md"),
        # Leading/trailing junk on the stem is stripped.
        ("  spaced out  .txt", "spaced-out.txt"),
        ("!!!bang.txt", "bang.txt"),
        # Unicode: NFKD normalization, then non-ascii dropped.
        ("café au lait.txt", "cafe-au-lait.txt"),
        ("naïve résumé.doc", "naive-resume.doc"),
        ("日本語 file.txt", "file.txt"),
        # Extension preserved exactly (only the stem is mangled).
        ("Weird Name.tar.gz", "weird-name.tar.gz"),
        # Dotfiles without an extension pass through unchanged.
        (".bashrc", ".bashrc"),
        (".profile", ".profile"),
        (".gitignore", ".gitignore"),
    ],
)
def test_sanitize(raw, expected):
    assert sanitize(raw) == expected


def test_check_clean_files_exits_zero():
    result = run_cli("--check", "clean.txt", "also-fine.zip")
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == ""


def test_check_dirty_file_exits_one():
    result = run_cli("--check", "Bad File!!.txt")
    assert result.returncode == 1
    assert result.stdout == ""


def test_check_any_dirty_input_triggers_failure():
    result = run_cli("--check", "clean.txt", "needs cleaning.csv")
    assert result.returncode == 1
    assert result.stdout == ""
